Sunbiz.org LLC filing (THE OAKS BARBERSHOP LLC, L22000080449): page blocked automated fetch (403); WebSearch snippet surfaced the registered agent's name (Jonathan G. Fuentes Ortiz) but no email.
Conclusion: no public email found after exhausting all listed sources. Outreach relies on phone call/text and Instagram DM to the barber's real account, @bravo.hairhustler787.
instagram_note: This is the real, active account linked directly from the Booksy business's own sameAs field (161 posts, 791 followers, bio: 'Florida barber... Professional barber since 2008'). It belongs to barber Jonathan 'Bravo' Fuentes, who a customer review explicitly identifies as working at 'Oaks Barbershop'. The handle originally guessed from discovery, @theoaksbarbershop, was checked and is a different, unrelated, inactive personal account (0 posts) -- NOT used anywhere.
own_site_check: CORRECTION to discovery assumption: theoaksbarbershop.com IS live and resolves (301 -> www.theoaksbarbershop.com, HTTP 200). It is a Square Online site (meta generator='Square Online', vertical 'salon-barbershop') on the business's own custom domain (not a *.square.site subdomain). It carries a genuine custom logo reading 'THE OAKS BARBERSHOP - EST. 2026' in navy/gold (confirms real ownership, not a generic template squat). However the site is extremely minimal: sitemap.xml lists only 4 generic product pages (haircut, haircut-beard-trim, kids-cut, waxing), zero configured brick-and-mortar/pickup locations in Square's own location data, and the page's configured site title / og:site_name is 'Jeremy Munson' (a personal name, not the shop name) with no address, phone, photos, reviews or about copy anywhere in the rendered/embedded JSON. Effectively a bare logo + 'Book' button. Per pipeline rules this counts as has_own_site: true, so the outreach angle is a premium redesign proposal, not 'you have no website'.

reviews_verbatim_full.body: Jonathan Bravo at Oaks Barbershop is hands down the best barber I've ever been to. From the moment I sat in his chair, he was incredibly gentle, professional, and had such a calm, balanced energy that immediately put me at ease. He's genuinely friendly and a true master of his craft. I came in with a specific vision, and he executed my request flawlessly. Every detail was perfect, and I walked out with the crispest haircut I've ever had. As a woman walking into a male-dominated barbershop, I wasn't sure what to expect, but Jonathan made me feel completely comfortable and welcomed from start to finish. That kind of professionalism and respect goes a long way. Honestly, he's so good that I'd take a plane from Rhode Island just to have him cut my hair again. If you're looking for a barber who combines incredible skill with amazing customer service, Jonathan Bravo is the one. Highly recommend!

photos.curation_notes: Visually reviewed every photo (contact sheet for the Booksy gallery pull, individually for IG and review photos) before selecting. Discarded: all 5 Booksy-gallery tiny avatars/placeholders (100x100/512x512, not real photos), 5 Instagram posts that were selfie-closeups, an unrelated group photo, an unrelated nighttime event photo, a corrupted black frame and a text-overlaid 'Before and after' video-poster frame, and 4 Booksy review photos that were plain customer selfies (car/bathroom mirror, no haircut visible). Kept only finished, well-lit, uncluttered shots: 2 real shop-interior action photos (barber cutting a client's hair, ring-light setup), 1 storefront exterior, 3 distinct finished-cut style photos (clean skin fade, curly fade, twists/locs updo), 2 kids' fade results (Batman design, mullet fade), 1 barber portrait (used small, as an about-section avatar only, never as a gallery tile), and the business's own logo.

notes: Major correction vs. the discovery seed: has_own_site is TRUE (theoaksbarbershop.com is live), not false as assumed. Also corrected the Instagram handle: @theoaksbarbershop (the guessed handle) is NOT the business; the real, active account is @bravo.hairhustler787, linked directly from Booksy's own sameAs field and confirmed by a customer review naming the barber.
